entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Adrian Józef Galbas SAC (born 1970) is a Polish Roman Catholic bishop and member of the Pallottine Fathers (Societas Apostolatus Catholici), appointed auxiliary bishop and later coadjutor of the Archdiocese of Katowice in Upper Silesia. His appointment reflects Pope Francis's priorities for the Polish Church — a Church marked by extraordinary religious vitality and institutional strength but also by the tensions between traditional Polish Catholicism and the Church's global reform agenda.

Poland's Catholic Church is one of Europe's most robustly practising national churches, with Mass attendance rates far above the Western European average and deep identification between Catholic faith and Polish national identity going back to the partitions era. Yet the Polish Church has also been challenged by clerical abuse scandals, generational change, and the political controversies arising from its close identification with the right-wing Law and Justice party.

Galbas's Pallottine formation emphasises missionary outreach and lay apostolate — priorities that align with Pope Francis's vision for a more missionary and synodal Church. His appointment as coadjutor of Katowice — one of Poland's most important industrial archdioceses — reflects an intention to bring a reform-oriented bishop to one of Polish Catholicism's key sees in Upper Silesia.

entities.summary: Adrian Józef Galbas, S.A.C. is a Polish prelate of the Catholic Church who has been Metropolitan Archbishop of Warsaw since December 2024. He became Archbishop of Katowice in May 2023, after sixteen months as coadjutor there. He was auxiliary bishop of Ełk from 2020 to 2021. He is a professed member of the Pallottines. Adrian Józef Galbas was a religious figures from Bytom (b. 1968-01-26, Bytom). A moderately significant entity in the historical record.
